description: One launch from a coastal site, taken from the instantaneous impact point through the public risk analysis to the flight termination system reliability claim. The trajectory states are representative of a two stage ascent to low orbit and the risk regions are the classic coastal geometry: a remote launch area, one town near the azimuth, and an ocean downrange.

trajectory.note: inertial speed and flight path angle above the local horizontal; the last row is at or past insertion

regions.name: coastal town
regions.crossNote: the town sits beside the ground track rather than under it, which is what a launch azimuth is chosen to arrange

risk.note: the impact probabilities are computed by DebrisDispersion from the fragment catalogue rather than assumed, which is what the start and end bands are for. They are left in the file as well so the computed and assumed sets can be printed side by side

termination.note: reliabilities per path and per series element; the single receiver case is the same ordnance behind one receiver

dispersion.note: the break-up state is the 60 second trajectory point above, which is the worst case for the coastal town: high enough for the light debris to be carried a long way and still steep enough for the heavy debris to run downrange
